_doc: Factory repo profile for insurance-app-base (FACTORY.md §2c). Every value here was verified by running or reading it in the Profiler run on issue #83. See templates/profile.schema.json in claude-software-factory for field docs.
estate_role: Standalone full-stack monorepo — the Spring Boot backend and the React/Vite frontend live in this one repo and ship as one Docker Compose unit. No sibling repos in this estate, so every epic is filed here and there is no cross-repo merge order to derive.
stack: Backend: Java 21 (source/target 21, requires a JDK 21 toolchain), Spring Boot 3.2.2, Spring Security + JWT (jjwt 0.12.5), Spring Data JPA, Spring AI 1.0.0-M4 (OpenAI chat/embeddings + pgvector store), Flyway 10, Lombok 1.18.36 + MapStruct 1.6.3, Twilio SDK, Apache Tika, OpenHTMLtoPDF, OpenCSV, springdoc-openapi, Micrometer/Prometheus, Maven. Frontend: React 18, TypeScript 5.3, Vite 5, Material-UI 5, TanStack Query 5, Zustand 4, react-hook-form, react-beautiful-dnd, axios, Vitest 1 + Testing Library. Database: PostgreSQL 16 with the pgvector extension (pgvector/pgvector:pg16). Infra: Docker + Docker Compose.

commands.test: cd backend && JAVA_HOME="${JAVA_HOME_21_X64:-$JAVA_HOME}" mvn -B test && cd ../frontend && npm ci && npm test
commands.build: cd backend && JAVA_HOME="${JAVA_HOME_21_X64:-$JAVA_HOME}" mvn -B clean package -DskipTests && cd ../frontend && npm ci && npm run build

conventions: Backend is organised by domain module under backend/src/main/java/com/insurance/{module}, each with controller/, dto/, service/, repository/ (plus mapper/ and exception/ where the module needs them). The modules are: auth, leads, products, scheduler, voice, rag, prospectus, email, admin.

JPA entities live only in common/entity/ and are shared across modules — never declare an entity inside a feature module, and never return one from a controller; controllers return DTOs from the module's dto/ package.

Controllers are @RestController + @RequestMapping("/api/...") + @RequiredArgsConstructor + @Slf4j, with constructor injection via final fields. Endpoints carry springdoc @Tag/@Operation/@Parameter annotations, take @Valid request bodies, and return ResponseEntity<T>.
Services are @Service + @RequiredArgsConstructor + @Slf4j and annotate read paths @Transactional(readOnly = true); business logic belongs here, not in controllers.
Repositories are Spring Data JPA interfaces annotated @Repository. Custom queries use @Query JPQL with @Param-bound parameters — never string-concatenated user input into the query structure.
Nullable String parameters in a JPQL @Query must be wrapped as CAST(:param AS string) (see ProductRepository.findByFilters) — see the bytea gotcha below.

Schema changes are a new forward-only Flyway migration at backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/V{next}__{description}.sql; never edit an applied migration. Current head is V13__add_phone_to_users.sql, so the next is V14.

Entity<->DTO conversion is either a MapStruct @Mapper(componentModel = "spring", unmappedTargetPolicy = ReportingPolicy.IGNORE) interface (leads/mapper/) or a private toDto() helper in the service (products/service/) — follow whichever the module you are editing already uses rather than introducing the other.

Frontend pages live under frontend/src/pages/agent/ or frontend/src/pages/admin/. A new page gets an axios client in frontend/src/api/, TypeScript types mirroring the backend DTO in frontend/src/types/index.ts, a route in App.tsx, and a Sidebar.tsx entry if it needs navigation.

All frontend HTTP goes through the shared axios instance in frontend/src/api/client.ts (baseURL '/api', bearer token from localStorage 'auth_token', 401 redirect) — do not create new axios instances. Per-domain modules export a plain object of async functions (e.g. productsApi.getAll).
Frontend server state goes through TanStack Query; auth/global UI state goes through the Zustand store in frontend/src/store/ — not ad hoc React context.
review_checklist: New or changed endpoints declare the @PreAuthorize the module already uses — hasRole('ADMIN') for admin-only, hasAnyRole('ADMIN','AGENT') for agent-facing. SecurityConfig only requires authentication for anything outside /api/auth/**, /actuator/**, / and /ping, so a missing annotation silently means 'any logged-in user'.

Agent-scoped reads must derive the agent from the Authentication, not trust a client-supplied agentId: LeadController computes an effectiveAgentId and forces it to the caller's own id unless the caller is ADMIN. A new lead/prospect query that skips this leaks other agents' leads.

products/controller/* (ProductController, ProductCategoryController, ProductDocumentController) currently carry NO @PreAuthorize — any authenticated user, agent included, can create/update/delete products. If a task touches these, treat adding authorization as a deliberate decision to raise, not an incidental change.
Any new table or column ships with a new V{n}__ Flyway migration rather than a rewrite of an existing one.
New @Query JPQL binds user input via @Param and wraps nullable String params in CAST(:p AS string).

org.springframework.web* logging levels stay at INFO in the committed defaults — DispatcherServlet logs the query string at DEBUG, which would write PII (?email=, ?search=) into the application log. Raise per-environment via WEB_LOG_LEVEL only.
No secrets, API keys or credential-bearing URLs in code, migrations, tests or docker-compose defaults.
RAG recommendation output stays grounded in retrieved product IDs (rag/service/RecommendationService maps embeddings back to real Product rows) rather than free-form LLM text.
qa_notes: Backend tests are JUnit 5 + AssertJ + Mockito under backend/src/test/java, mirroring the main package layout, and named after the behaviour under test (e.g. ProductRepositoryNameFilterTest). Related cases are grouped in @Nested inner classes with @DisplayName. 99 tests exist across auth, products and admin.

Backend test layering, as practised in the existing suites: service tests mock the repository; controller tests use @WebMvcTest-style Spring slices with MockMvc and cover authorization plus request-parameter binding; repository tests use @DataJpaTest against a real database.

Repository tests use Testcontainers, NOT H2: @DataJpaTest builds the persistence unit from every entity in common/entity/, which uses jsonb, vector(1536) and text[] — none of which H2 can model. They start PostgreSQLContainer on pgvector/pgvector:pg16 with .withInitScript("db/init/01-init-pgvector.sql") and wire it in with @ServiceConnection. That init script is required: V4__create_vector_embeddings_table.sql uses vector(1536) but no migration creates the extension, so Flyway fails at V4 without it. com.h2database:h2 is still declared test-scoped in backend/pom.xml but no test uses it — do not take its presence as a signal that H2 is the test database.

Repository tests therefore need a running Docker daemon. Where Docker is unavailable they are the only tests that cannot run; service and controller tests still cover normalisation, binding and authorization.

backend/src/test/resources/application.properties sets spring.ai.openai.api-key=test — application.yml's one placeholder with no default. Any new test that loads the AI configuration needs it to stay.

Frontend tests are Vitest + React Testing Library + user-event, colocated with the component as <Component>.test.tsx. jsdom environment and globals are configured in vite.config.ts; frontend/src/test/setup.ts imports @testing-library/jest-dom/vitest.
Frontend tests mock the api/ module with vi.mock and render the page inside a QueryClientProvider built with retry:false — see ProductManagement.test.tsx as the reference pattern.
Voice flows should be exercised with VOICE_MOCK_MODE=true (the application.yml default) so no real OpenAI Realtime or Twilio calls are made.
gotchas: The build needs JDK 21. maven-compiler-plugin 3.13.0 is configured <source>21</source><target>21</target> (not <release>), and the GitHub runner's default JAVA_HOME is Temurin 17 — a clean `mvn compile`/`mvn test` under JDK 17 fails with 'error: release version 21 not supported'. Note an incremental `mvn compile` over an already-built target/ can still print BUILD SUCCESS under JDK 17 because there is nothing to recompile; that is not evidence the JDK is adequate. That is why the test/build commands above set JAVA_HOME from JAVA_HOME_21_X64; this is an environment requirement, not a code defect.

KNOWN_ISSUES.md documents a Lombok failure ('java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError: com.sun.tools.javac.code.TypeTag :: UNKNOWN') on OpenJDK 21.0.5 Temurin specifically. It did NOT reproduce on Temurin 21.0.12, where the full suite passes. If you hit that signature, it is the JDK build, not the delta — switch JDK rather than changing code.

Admin settings are NOT really encrypted. AdminSettingService.encrypt/decrypt are plain Base64 (the code says so: 'In production, use proper encryption like AES'), despite README/CLAUDE.md describing settings as encrypted. Do not rely on that column to protect a secret, and do not describe it as encryption in new work.

Nullable String parameters in JPQL must be CAST(:p AS string) on PostgreSQL. Hibernate otherwise infers bytea for a null-valued String parameter and the query fails at runtime — fixed once already in ProductRepository.findByFilters (commit 99fba33, 'fix: bind findByFilters String params typed to stop bytea coercion'). Repeating the untyped pattern reintroduces the bug, and only the Testcontainers repository tests catch it.

`npm run lint` is defined in frontend/package.json but cannot run: there is no ESLint config anywhere in the repo (no .eslintrc*, no eslint.config.*, no eslintConfig key), so ESLint 8.57 exits 2 with 'ESLint couldn't find a configuration file'. That is why commands.lint is null. Type checking still happens — `npm run build` runs tsc before vite build.

CLAUDE.md and README.md describe CI/CD workflows (ci.yml, cd.yml, deploy.yml) that do not exist. .github/workflows/ contains only factory-pipeline.yml and factory-branch-guard.yml. There is no CI, no staging branch and no deploy automation in this repo — do not assume a pipeline will catch anything you did not run yourself.
CLAUDE.md says the latest migration is V11 and the next is V12; it is actually V13, next V14. Trust the migration directory over the docs.

Swagger UI and /api-docs are disabled by default in application.yml (springdoc.api-docs.enabled=false, springdoc.swagger-ui.enabled=false) even though SecurityConfig permits their paths — they are not reachable without flipping those flags.

The default seed credentials (admin@insurance.com / Admin@123, agent@insurance.com / Agent@123) come from the V10/V11 migrations and are dev-only seed data — never treat them as secrets to rotate, and never let them reach a real deployment.
The frontend production bundle is a single ~612 kB chunk and Vite warns about it on every build. That warning is pre-existing baseline noise, not something your delta introduced.

notes: These are the local/Compose checks — the only ones this repo gives evidence for. There is no deploy workflow, no staging branch and no known staging or production hostname in the repo, so substitute the real host if one exists rather than assuming these URLs reach a deployed environment.

The actuator health check mirrors docker-compose.yml's own backend healthcheck; management.endpoints.web.exposure.include lists health, info, metrics, prometheus and mappings, and SecurityConfig permits /actuator/** unauthenticated. health show-details is when-authorized, so an unauthenticated curl returns status only.
The frontend container serves the built bundle via nginx on port 80, published as FRONTEND_PORT (default 3000).

Postgres must come up with the pgvector extension before the backend: db/init/01-init-pgvector.sql is mounted into the image's entrypoint directory, and without it Flyway fails at V4__create_vector_embeddings_table.sql and the backend never starts. A backend that will not start after a database replacement is almost always this.
The backend requires OPENAI_API_KEY, JWT_SECRET and the DB credentials to be set; spring.ai.openai.api-key has no default and the context fails without it.
